question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Gross margin (GAAP))

calls.reasoning: On the Q2 FY27 call (Aug 26, 2026) CFO Kress said gross margin would bottom out at 71-72% in Q4 FY27, GAAP and non-GAAP alike, because of memory costs, then recover to 72-73% in FY28. Recent guides have had identical GAAP and non-GAAP numbers (Q3: 74.0% +/-50bp) with round midpoints, so the modal outcome is 71.5% (or 71.0%/72.0%). Downside: memory prices are 'headed even higher', and GAAP may again sit a few tenths below non-GAAP. Upside: price increases could come earlier, and NVDA has tended to meet or beat its margin commentary. Market check: no market prices the Q4 guide; Polymarket's Q3 actual non-GAAP GM markets (73-75% at 0.85, low volume) are a near-miss contract and only confirm the Q3 path.
calls.dossier:
- Q2 FY27 press release (Aug 26, 2026): Q2 GAAP GM 75.0% and non-GAAP 75.0%; Q3 FY27 outlook GAAP and non-GAAP GM 74.0% +/-50bp; revenue $108.0B +/-2%.
- Q2 FY27 call (Aug 26, 2026; per Yahoo Finance and bit.fan write-ups): CFO Kress said GM would bottom out at 71-72% in Q4 FY27 for both GAAP and non-GAAP, then recover to 72-73% in FY28; price adjustments take effect in Q1 FY28.
- Kress quote from the same call: 'extreme pricing conditions in memory... exceeded our prior expectations and are headed even higher into next year.' Supply commitments rose from $119B to $279B, mostly memory.
- The same call also mentioned working on cost, cycle time and mix to 'hold' GM in the mid-70s over time (longer-term aim).
- Format history: NVDA guides GM as a single midpoint +/-50bp, usually ending in .0 or .5 (e.g. 74.0, 75.0; Q4 FY26 was GAAP 74.8 / non-GAAP 75.0). GAAP has sometimes been 0.2-0.3pp below non-GAAP, but the last two quarters were identical.
- IG preview (Nov 10, 2026): repeats the 71-72% Q4 warning; Q3 report due Nov 17, 2026.
- News Nov 11-12, 2026: WSJ reports the board is weighing removing CEO Huang (unverified by Reuters); not a direct margin driver.
- Status quo: Q4 guide consistent with the stated 71-72% bottom.
- Resolves off the GAAP gross-margin midpoint in the 'Outlook' section of the Q3 FY27 press release (Nov 17, 2026), rounded to 0.1%; not off non-GAAP figures and not off call commentary.
- Event window: single release on Nov 17, 2026; as of Nov 12, 2026, 0% elapsed (pending).
- Searched for but did not find: any update to the Q4 margin commentary between the Aug call and Nov 12, 2026; consensus Q4 GM estimates; a market on the Q4 guide (only Polymarket markets on Q3 actual non-GAAP GM exist).

calls.reasoning: The anchor is CFO Kress's Q2 FY27 statement (Aug 26, 2026) that gross margin will decline and bottom out at 71-72% in Q4 FY27, driven by memory, packaging and manufacturing costs, then recover to 72-73% in FY28 as price increases take effect. NVIDIA has recently guided GAAP and non-GAAP margins identically (Q3 guide: 74.0% for both), so the GAAP Q4 guide most likely has a midpoint of 71.5%. If memory-cost pressure eases or the Q3 result beats, it could be 72.0. If memory pricing gets worse, it could slip to 71.0 or lower. The Huang governance scandal has no direct bearing on gross margin guidance. Polymarket only has contracts on Q3 non-GAAP actual margin (73-75% at about 85%, thin volume). That is a different quantity, but it is consistent with Q3 landing near its 74% guide and gives no sign of a margin collapse. I found no market on the Q4 guide itself.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same anchor (71-72% Q4 bottom from the Aug 26 call) and give a 71.5 median. Factual dispute: whether Huang resigned (Run 3) or the board is only weighing his removal (Runs 1-2). I could not settle this without web access; either version affects GM guidance only through possible conservatism, so it adds slight downside skew rather than moving the median. GAAP/non-GAAP gap: the dossiers show it has collapsed to about 0 ($46M of adjustments), so it is not material. The tail width is a judgment call; I kept Runs 1-2's dispersion with a slightly wider lower tail for the memory-cost risk.
